item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract. It provides the exact Upload signature, reuses multipartbody.NewFile, preserves FilesOption handling, and avoids A’s prohibited association-option API and multipart helper expansion.","reasons":["B implements the required signature exactly: Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption). A instead introduces UploadFileOption, making its public API contractually incompatible.","B reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile as required. A adds NewForm and substantial duplicate option/form-field machinery.","A explicitly adds association fields and WithUpload* options, despite the contract forbidding association fields and requiring FilesOption behavior to remain unchanged.","B applies existing FilesOption query and request options. A’s new option family prevents callers from using existing FilesOption values with Upload and changes option semantics unnecessarily as well as enlarging the API surface considerably."],"risks_a":["Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates request construction, response decoding, and missing-data handling.","The added association API and multipart NewForm helper are out of scope and increase maintenance burden.","No visible test covers source-reader failures, although propagation is required."],"risks_b":["Upload still calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing the encoded body through FilesService.Add, duplicating logic the contract requires to remain centralized.","Its retry test uses strings.NewReader rather than a genuinely non-seekable streamed source, so it does not strongly verify that buffering makes streamed content replayable.","No visible test covers source-reader errors."]}
